visualGuidance.role: Approved inline style reference for broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours and minimal texture; supplied as image input.
Chie's character identity and palette only; supplied as image input.

scenes.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: landscape inline story painting for the graded-reader “The Earth That Stays Put”
Primary request: depict the end of paragraph 1: Chie and her mother set off in their lunar rover before the long night, and Chie looks back to see the blue Earth above the base.
Input images: Image 1 is the approved inline style reference only; Image 2 guides Chie's character identity and palette only.
Scene/backdrop: quiet grey lunar hills around a small base and a few simple solar panels beneath a deep black sky; the blue Earth hangs above the base.
Subject: a compact practical rover travels away from the Moon base. Chie, a twelve-year-old girl with dark hair tied back, wears the simple blue-grey uniform from the cover and turns to look back through the rover's open side. Her mother drives. Keep both calm and readable, with no helmet indoors.
Style/medium: gentle children's picture-book painting in the approved Kasa Jizō inline treatment: broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours, minimal texture, a few purposeful folds and shadows, quiet simplified background; distinctly simpler than the textured cover.
Composition/framing: medium-wide landscape about 12:7; rover and two people in the foreground, base and blue Earth clear but secondary in the distance; two or three broad depth layers.
Lighting/mood: cool late-afternoon light before lunar night, thoughtful and calm.
Color palette: warm ivory, midnight indigo, muted teal, soft grey, with the Earth as a restrained blue accent.
Constraints: portray only the departure and Chie's backward glance from paragraph 1. Do not hint that anyone will become lost. No lettering, signs, labels, title, border, frame, or watermark.
Avoid: stranded rover, blank screen, lost characters, radio distress, rescue, photorealism, glossy 3D, dense brush texture, busy background.

Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: landscape inline story painting for the graded-reader “The Earth That Stays Put”
Primary request: show the end of paragraph 0: Chie looks through her bedroom window on the Moon and sees the blue Earth hanging above the same grey hill.
Input images: Image 1 is the story cover, for Chie’s identity and muted uniform palette only; Images 2–4 are approved Kasa Jizō inline paintings, for broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours and minimal surface texture only.
Scene/backdrop: a simple Moon-base bedroom window overlooks one softly layered grey hill. The sky beyond is black; the blue Earth appears above the hill, and a few old rover tyre tracks cross the quiet foreground.
Subject: Chie is a twelve-year-old girl with dark hair tied back and a simple blue-grey uniform matching the cover. Show her calmly looking at the Earth through the window, in a clear side view. Keep her natural and small within the landscape.
Style/medium: gentle children’s picture-book painting in the approved Kasa Jizō inline treatment: broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours, minimal surface texture, a few purposeful folds and shadows, quiet simplified background; distinctly simpler than the textured cover.
Composition/framing: landscape about 12:7 for the reader, medium-wide; Chie and the window form the foreground focus, with the hill and Earth clearly readable beyond, two or three broad depth layers.
Lighting/mood: soft interior light against the sunlit lunar surface, quiet and observant.
Color palette: warm ivory, midnight indigo, muted teal, soft lunar grey and restrained Earth blue.
Constraints: depict only paragraph 0. The Earth appears in the same sky position above the same hill. No lettering, labels, title, border, frame or watermark.
Avoid: rover departure, lost rover, blank screen, distress, extra people, busy room clutter, photorealism, glossy 3D, dense brush texture, highly detailed background.

Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: landscape inline story painting for the graded-reader “The Earth That Stays Put”
Primary request: show the end of paragraph 4: Chie remembers where the base lay relative to the fixed Earth and points her mother toward it from the rover.
Input images: Image 1 is the story cover, for Chie’s identity and muted uniform palette only; Images 2–4 are approved Kasa Jizō inline paintings, for broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours and minimal surface texture only.
Scene/backdrop: a simple view inside a compact lunar rover, with a broad windscreen showing a grey hill and the blue Earth fixed above it in the black sky. Keep the instrument panel quiet and mostly dark.
Subject: Chie, twelve, has dark hair tied back and wears the same simple blue-grey uniform. She points through the windscreen toward the Earth while speaking with her mother, who is driving and has begun to turn the steering wheel in that direction. Their faces show focused recognition, not panic.
Style/medium: gentle children’s picture-book painting in the approved Kasa Jizō inline treatment: broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours, minimal surface texture, a few purposeful folds and shadows, quiet simplified background; distinctly simpler than the textured cover.
Composition/framing: landscape about 12:7 for the reader, medium-wide interior view; Chie’s pointing hand, the mother at the controls and the Earth beyond the windscreen are clear, with two or three broad depth layers.
Lighting/mood: cool, calm lunar daylight with the blue Earth as the quiet focal point.
Color palette: warm ivory, midnight indigo, muted teal, soft lunar grey and restrained Earth blue.
Constraints: depict only paragraph 4, before they find the base. Exactly one mother and one child in one rover. No lettering, labels, title, border, frame or watermark.
Avoid: rescue, base lights, people outside, panic, injury, extra characters, photorealism, glossy 3D, dense brush texture, highly detailed background.
